label: Security watch: what it checks, how often it must have run, which findings turn the bar red

params.name: record
params.label: Store name of the last watch's answer (body-free: package names, file:line, check names)

params.name: block_severities
params.label: Severities that turn the owner's bar red and stop a ship

params.name: unknown_severity
params.label: A known vulnerability whose advisory names no severity counts as this (never as nothing)

params.name: locks
params.label: Hash lock files read (paths from the portal folder; a missing one is skipped)

params.name: osv_hosts
params.label: Hosts the watch may fetch (core/egress allow-list)

params.name: max_advisories
params.label: Most advisories read in one run (the rest count at unknown_severity)

params.name: every_days
params.label: The schedule: days between watches (the agent's trigger says week)

params.name: grace_days
params.label: Days past every_days before the bar says the watch is overdue

params.name: ledger_kind
params.label: Ledger security-event kind for one watch run (counts only)

params.name: agent
params.label: The agent that runs the watch

params.name: lower_shown
params.label: Lower (not blocking) findings kept in the record

description_nl: 2026-11-19 owner: "Every week (or based on schedule) verify the software vulnerability and fix". The agent ag_security_watch (its trigger is the schedule) checks every pinned package against osv.dev (the database pip-audit and npm audit read), the secret scan, the route guards, the CSP, the egress ratchet, the lowest Python, the restore drill; core/securitywatch.py keeps the answer in `record`, the health bar shows each blocking finding.
